title: What dates fill the blank cells of a calendar grid?
description: A grid of two rows and three columns is taken from a calendar, and the bottom middle date is the letter w. The video writes the other five dates as expressions in w and checks them with fifteen.
teaching_notes: One idea: on a calendar one step right is one more, and one row up is seven less, so every cell is w plus or minus a number. Watch for students who think the row above is only one less.

video_script.why: A learner uses a letter for the unknown date and writes the neighbouring dates by adding or taking away, as the bill expression adds amounts.
video_script.substitution: The method of the bill expression, with a letter w for one date and plus or minus for its neighbours.
video_script.anchor: a grid of two rows and three columns cut from a calendar month
video_script.payoff_line: The bottom row is w minus one, w, and w plus one

final_answer.value: Top row: w − 8, w − 7, w − 6. Bottom row: w − 1, w, w + 1
final_answer.spoken: the top row is w minus eight, w minus seven and w minus six, and the bottom row is w minus one, w and w plus one

never_show: the five finished expressions before the answer beat
maths_rules: On a calendar, the date to the right is 1 more and the date to the left is 1 less.
The date in the row above is 7 less, because a week has 7 days.
Check with w = 15: bottom row 14, 15, 16 and top row 7, 8, 9.
video_script.design: One idea: right is one more, left is one less, and up is seven less. Assumes the bill expression. The grid stays on the stage with the cell w highlighted. No wrong idea is raised.
